Micro E-mini S&P 500 (MES futures, Dec 2026): new plan.
Levels use the plan's prices.
If price trades into 7,520–7,530, the desk is bullish on the S&P 500 over the period to Thu 12 Nov, 07:00 ET. Invalidated if price moves below 7,480.
Why:
• Base case 52% (Capital Chronicle model estimate): the S&P 500 holds above 7,500 and extends the 9 Nov squeeze beyond the 7,581.97 post-event high within three sessions.
• Main alternative 38% (Capital Chronicle model estimate): a hot CPI seals a December Fed hike, the day-one squeeze fails and the S&P 500 falls back through 7,500 toward the old 7,446 ceiling.

• Mechanism: a global risk impulse, lower oil plus covering of an index short. Asia holds 7,556-7,567 and Nikkei futures rose 3.2%. the S&P 500 is a net transmitter in the connectedness row (+0.24).

• What is priced: drift +1.38 ATR from the 6 Nov close of 7,383.33 to the

7,561.65 capture; one-day move 1.81 volatility-normalised; 20-day mean 7,618.2 (z -0.44), 50-day 7,681.8 (z -1.10), 200-day 7,450.3 (z +0.33); 20-day range 7,300.5-7,792.4; ATR 128.9 at the 99.4th percentile; VIX closed 19.92 on 9 Nov, an implied daily move near 95 points; prior

pricing AMBIGUOUS.

• Positioning: E-mini non-commercial net short 129,414, 6.5% of open interest, dated 3 Nov before the 5 Nov crash (a weak squeeze gauge); the negative GEX proxy dated 23 Oct means dealer hedging amplifies a break either way.
• Today's driver: mixed (oil, de-escalation and chips other than Nvidia against hike risk and the Nvidia probe).

• Reaction so far: the rally held into the close (7,562.9 against the 7,581.97 high), but on a mixed channel a day-one move is unconfirmed (4 Nov lesson), so continuation belongs beyond 7,581.97 and a test of that extreme is expected.

• Why this zone: pullback zone

7,520.00-7,530.00 at the first post-breakout base (9 Nov 11:00 ET H1 low 7,519.48, bar open 2026-11-09T16:00Z, known 2026-11-10T00:24:30.309Z; breakout zone 7,586.00-7,596.00 above the nearest resistance, the 9 Nov 15:00 ET H1 high of 7,581.97 (same evidence and clock).

• What confirms it: (1) the hold of the 7,445.67 breakout into the close in the the S&P 500 H1 and M15 bars; (2) the cross-asset risk impulse in the native-intraday frames (the Nasdaq 100 +4.13%, oil lower).

• Alternative mechanism: a hot CPI seals a December hike and the day-one squeeze fails; the Nvidia probe hits AI capex sentiment.; Crowd trade (G05 5): chasing the short-covering rally, wrong on a hot CPI or Nvidia news.
Analysis, not financial advice. Capital Chronicle may hold positions in the markets it covers.
